questions.q: In the Hercules parable, what does Virtue promise to those who take her path?
a: Rewards earned through courage and hardship
A life of pleasure without any pain
Wealth and fame without much effort
Wisdom granted at the moment of birth
questions.why: The overview contrasts Vice's painless pleasure with Virtue's offer of rewards you earn through effort.

questions.q: Why does the summary say discipline is easiest to build through your body first?
a: You can feel the results of your efforts
Physical tasks require the least willpower
Your body responds faster than your mind
Others can see and praise your progress
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that physical challenges give you felt feedback that the discipline is working.

questions.q: What matters most when building physical discipline, according to the summary?
a: Doing a little every day rather than a lot occasionally
Training hard for a few weeks each year
Following a strict program without any breaks
Waiting until you feel fully motivated
questions.why: Lesson 1 stresses showing up consistently over rare bursts of intense effort, using Lou Gehrig as an example.

questions.q: Why does the summary say we need restraint to enjoy life's pleasures?
a: Doing something constantly makes it meaningless
Pleasure is only available to disciplined people
Too much joy leads to physical illness
Restraint makes pleasures last longer in memory
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that indulging every impulse drains the enjoyment out of things, so moderation is required.

questions.q: What gives discipline its point, according to the summary's third lesson?
a: Using it for the greater good
Winning recognition from others
Achieving perfect self-control
Escaping all outside obligations
questions.why: Lesson 3 says discipline is pointless unless it serves a higher purpose and is paired with kindness.
